vocabulary.definition: a sudden and violent collapse inward
vocabulary.example: If the fertility rate remains low, South Korea will experience a population implosion within the next century.

vocabulary.definition: the reduction in the number of people in a specific region or country
vocabulary.example: Eastern Europe has experienced depopulation due to many young people emigrating to stronger economies.

vocabulary.definition: dislike or prejudice against people from other countries
vocabulary.example: Immigration policies can sometimes lead to increased xenophobia in societies.

vocabulary.definition: the statistical data of a population, especially those showing average age, income, education, etc.
vocabulary.example: Understanding demographics is crucial for governments to plan for the future of their countries.

vocabulary.definition: not conforming to accepted standards of morality
vocabulary.example: Keeping poor countries poor to encourage migration is seen as an immoral strategy.

vocabulary.definition: able to be maintained at a certain rate or level
vocabulary.example: Long-term immigration may not be sustainable as birth rates are declining worldwide.
